title: Move to Millions: The Proven Framework to Become a Million Dollar CEO with Grace & Ease Instead of Hustle & Grind
author: Dr. Darnyelle Jervey Harmon
target_audience: Small business owners and entrepreneurs aiming to scale beyond six figures
Women and minority entrepreneurs seeking representation and practical strategies
Professionals desiring a holistic, values-based approach to wealth
Individuals looking for sustainable business growth without burnout
core_themes: Scaling from six to seven figures sustainably
Faith, purpose, and integrity in entrepreneurship
Building businesses with systems, not just hustle
primary_purpose: To provide entrepreneurs with a clear, actionable roadmap to build million-dollar businesses rooted in alignment, faith, and ease—rehabilitating the traditional hustle-and-grind mindset with a more sustainable, spiritually grounded approach.

structure_format.narrative_style: Empowering, conversational, and candid, blending personal stories with practical strategies
structure_format.organization: Divided into themed sections outlining the MOVE To Millions framework and specific growth steps
features: Personal anecdotes and client success case studies
Emphasis on both mindset and practical business operations

key_concepts_lessons: Sustainable business growth begins with a mindset shift, moving away from hustle culture.
Faith, belief in oneself, and clarity of purpose are essential drivers for reaching seven figures.
Systems and infrastructure are as important as marketing and sales for long-term scale.
Building wealth is about legacy, alignment, and enjoying the process, not just financial results.
Entrepreneurial success requires self-care, healthy boundaries, and values-based decision-making.
notable_features: Faith-based, unapologetic discussion of spirituality in business
Blend of mindset work and business systems
Focus on underrepresented entrepreneurs, especially women of color
cultural_historical_context: Written in the post-pandemic era when many entrepreneurs are rethinking hustle culture while seeking financial and personal fulfillment; the book addresses the needs of women and minority business owners seeking representation and spiritual integration in business advice.
reception_impact: Praised for its authenticity and holistic approach to scaling businesses
Celebrated by readers for merging faith, mindset, and tactical business growth strategies
Valued by women and underrepresented entrepreneurs for representation and relatability
Critics may find it less applicable if uninterested in faith-based frameworks
comparable_titles: We Should All Be Millionaires by Rachel Rodgers
The Million Dollar One Person Business by Elaine Pofeldt
Daring Greatly by Brené Brown (for mindset and vulnerability aspects)
